the guide

What is CoderBaba?

CoderBaba is a free, open-source AI coding agent that runs in your terminal. You describe what you want in plain English, such as "add rate limiting to the webhook endpoint" or "migrate this component to the new API," and CoderBaba does the work. It reads your codebase, plans the change, edits files, runs commands and verifies the result with your own tests.

It isn't an autocomplete plugin or a chat window that pastes snippets. It's a complete tool for building software from the command line, whether that's a new feature, a bug fix, a refactor, a script or an entire project from an empty folder.

Then open any project and describe your first task:

CoderBaba works best inside a git repository, because that's how it keeps parallel tasks isolated and every change reviewable.

How CoderBaba works

  1. Understand. CoderBaba maps the parts of your codebase that matter for the task: structure, dependencies, conventions and the files involved.
  2. Plan. It outlines the change before writing code, so multi-file edits stay consistent.
  3. Act. It edits files, creates new ones and runs commands in your project, showing each step as it happens.
  4. Verify. It runs your tests, type checker and linter, then fixes what fails and tries again.
  5. Hand off. You get a diff and a summary. Approve it, reject it or ask for changes.

Because every task runs in its own git worktree, you can start several at once. Each one has its own branch and files, so parallel work never collides.

Why open models, and why open source

Free to use. CoderBaba is free, whether you run models on your own machine or in our cloud.

Any open-source model. Pick the model that fits the task. Use a large agentic model such as Qwen3-Coder for complex work, a fast model for quick edits, or Devstral for a capable agent that fits on one GPU.

Local when you want it. Run a model on your own hardware and your code never leaves your machine, which matters for teams under NDAs, in regulated industries or with sensitive intellectual property.

Open source, permanently. You can read exactly how CoderBaba builds prompts, which files it reads and what it sends to a model. No company can take it away, change the terms or shut it down on you.

Quality has caught up. Open models such as Qwen2.5-Coder 32B matched GPT-4o on several code benchmarks at release. Agentic models like Qwen3-Coder and Devstral were trained specifically to fix real GitHub issues end to end.

Choosing a model for CoderBaba

CoderBaba runs any open-source model, and our model guide covers the major ones in depth. Four questions will narrow it down. Our full guide to choosing a model goes deeper on each.

  1. What's the task? Multi-step agent work benefits from models trained for tool use and long tasks. Quick, focused edits can use a smaller, faster model.
  2. Local or cloud? In our cloud, hardware isn't your problem. Locally, a rough rule is that a model at 4-bit quantization needs a bit over half a gigabyte of memory per billion parameters, plus room for context. A 7B model fits in 8 GB, and a 32B model wants about 24 GB.
  3. How much context do you need? Repository-level work benefits from models with 128K tokens or more.
  4. Will you ship the model's output commercially? Licenses vary. Every model page shows a clear commercial-use badge.

A fast all-rounderQwen2.5-Coder 14B or 32B
Broad language coverageDeepSeek-Coder-V2
Transparent, documented training dataStarCoder2 or Granite Code

What people build with CoderBaba

  • New features from a one-line description, including the tests
  • Bug fixes where CoderBaba reproduces the failure, finds the cause and proves the fix
  • Refactors and migrations across dozens of files, such as framework upgrades or API changes
  • Scripts, tools and prototypes built from scratch in an empty folder
  • Test coverage for code that never had any
  • Parallel workstreams, with several tasks running side by side in separate worktrees

Coming from another tool?

If you used Conductor, CoderBaba's one-task-per-worktree model will feel familiar. Our Conductor alternative guide explains how to back up your cloud workspaces before the shutdown and move your workflow over.

the guide

What is CoderBaba?

CoderBaba is a free, open-source AI coding agent that runs in your terminal. You describe what you want in plain English, such as "add rate limiting to the webhook endpoint" or "migrate this component to the new API," and CoderBaba does the work. It reads your codebase, plans the change, edits files, runs commands and verifies the result with your own tests.

It isn't an autocomplete plugin or a chat window that pastes snippets. It's a complete tool for building software from the command line, whether that's a new feature, a bug fix, a refactor, a script or an entire project from an empty folder.

CoderBaba works best inside a git repository, because that's how it keeps parallel tasks isolated and every change reviewable.

How CoderBaba works

  1. Understand. CoderBaba maps the parts of your codebase that matter for the task: structure, dependencies, conventions and the files involved.
  2. 计划。 It outlines the change before writing code, so multi-file edits stay consistent.
  3. Act. It edits files, creates new ones and runs commands in your project, showing each step as it happens.
  4. 核实。 It runs your tests, type checker and linter, then fixes what fails and tries again.
  5. 不可触摸。 You get a diff and a summary. Approve it, reject it or ask for changes.

Because every task runs in its own git worktree, you can start several at once. Each one has its own branch and files, so parallel work never collides.

Why open models, and why open source

免费使用。 CoderBaba is free, whether you run models on your own machine or in our cloud.

Any open-source model. Pick the model that fits the task. Use a large agentic model such as Qwen3-Coder for complex work, a fast model for quick edits, or Devstral for a capable agent that fits on one GPU.

Local when you want it. Run a model on your own hardware and your code never leaves your machine, which matters for teams under NDAs, in regulated industries or with sensitive intellectual property.

Open source, permanently. You can read exactly how CoderBaba builds prompts, which files it reads and what it sends to a model. No company can take it away, change the terms or shut it down on you.

Quality has caught up. Open models such as Qwen2.5-Coder 32B matched GPT-4o on several code benchmarks at release. Agentic models like Qwen3-Coder and Devstral were trained specifically to fix real GitHub issues end to end.

Choosing a model for CoderBaba

CoderBaba runs any open-source model, and our model guide covers the major ones in depth. Four questions will narrow it down. Our full guide to choosing a model goes deeper on each.

  1. What's the task? Multi-step agent work benefits from models trained for tool use and long tasks. Quick, focused edits can use a smaller, faster model.
  2. Local or cloud? In our cloud, hardware isn't your problem. Locally, a rough rule is that a model at 4-bit quantization needs a bit over half a gigabyte of memory per billion parameters, plus room for context. A 7B model fits in 8 GB, and a 32B model wants about 24 GB.
  3. How much context do you need? Repository-level work benefits from models with 128K tokens or more.
  4. Will you ship the model's output commercially? Licenses vary. Every model page shows a clear commercial-use badge.

What people build with CoderBaba

  • New features from a one-line description, including the tests
  • Bug fixes where CoderBaba reproduces the failure, finds the cause and proves the fix
  • Refactors and migrations across dozens of files, such as framework upgrades or API changes
  • Scripts, tools and prototypes built from scratch in an empty folder
  • Test coverage for code that never had any
  • Parallel workstreams, with several tasks running side by side in separate worktrees
